title: MYTP01 for Immune-Mediated Diseases
off: A Multicenter, Prospective Basket Clinical Trial of AI-Selected Traditional Chinese Medicine for Immune-Mediated Diseases and Investigation of Its Immunomodulatory Mechanisms
summary:
The goal of this study is to evaluate whether MYTP01, a traditional Chinese herbal formula developed by clinical experts with the assistance of artificial intelligence (AI), is effective and safe as an additional treatment for immune-mediated diseases (post-kidney transplantation, IgA nephropathy, etc.). The study also aims to explore whether MYTP01 may provide therapeutic benefits across these conditions by regulating shared immune and inflammatory processes. The main questions this study aims to answer are:

* Does MYTP01 provide clinical benefits and remain safe when used as an additional treatment for immune-mediated conditions?
* Does MYTP01 help regulate immune balance and inflammatory responses across immune-mediated disease populations?

Researchers will compare MYTP01 with a matching placebo, with both treatments given in addition to standard medical care, to evaluate clinical efficacy, safety, and potential immunomodulatory effects across immune-mediated conditions.

Participants will:

* Be enrolled in a disease-specific cohort based on their clinical condition.
* Be randomly assigned to receive either MYTP01 or placebo in addition to their usual medical treatment.
* Take the assigned study treatment twice daily for 8 weeks.
* Attend follow-up visits approximately once a month during a 12-week study period.
* Undergo clinical assessments, blood and urine tests, and evaluations of immune function and possible side effects.
desc:
This study is designed to evaluate the clinical value of MYTP01, a traditional Chinese herbal formula developed by clinical experts with the assistance of artificial intelligence (AI), as an adjunct to standard medical treatment for representative immune-mediated conditions (post-kidney transplantation, IgA nephropathy, etc.). The study aims to investigate whether MYTP01 may provide therapeutic benefits across different immune-mediated conditions by modulating shared immune and inflammatory processes.

The trial adopts a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled basket design. Approximately 160 participants are enrolled into two disease-specific cohorts based on their clinical conditions. After screening and baseline assessments, eligible participants within each cohort are randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive either MYTP01 or a matching placebo in addition to standard medical treatment.

All participants continue their standard medical treatment, including immunosuppressive therapy as prescribed, throughout the study period. Participants receive oral MYTP01 or placebo twice daily for 8 weeks, followed by continued follow-up until approximately Day 90. Clinical assessments are performed at predefined time points to monitor clinical outcomes, immune function, and treatment safety.

Clinical efficacy is evaluated through changes in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), 24-hour urinary protein excretion, and traditional Chinese medicine syndrome scores. Potential immunomodulatory effects are further explored by assessing T-lymphocyte subsets and inflammatory cytokines, including IL-2, IL-6, IL-10, TNF-α, and TGF-β, to investigate immune and inflammatory responses across the representative disease cohorts.

Standardized clinical and laboratory assessments are performed across participating centers to ensure consistency in data collection and outcome evaluation. Safety is continuously monitored through clinical examinations, routine laboratory testing, and the recording of adverse events throughout the treatment and follow-up periods.

The results of this study are expected to provide preliminary clinical evidence regarding the efficacy, safety, and potential immunomodulatory effects of MYTP01 in representative immune-mediated conditions. The findings may also help evaluate the feasibility of AI-assisted traditional Chinese herbal formula development and inform future investigations of shared therapeutic strategies across immune-mediated diseases.
elig:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Adults aged 18 to 65 years.
* Diagnosed with one of the following conditions: (1) Kidney transplant recipients: At least 6 months after kidney transplantation, with stable graft function (eGFR variation \<20% and no recent acute rejection). (2) IgA nephropathy: Biopsy-confirmed primary IgA nephropathy within the past 5 years, with persistent disease activity despite at least 3 months of supportive treatment (UPCR 0.5-3.5 g/day and eGFR ≥ 30 mL/min/1.73 m²).
* Stable immunosuppressive or other background medical treatment for at least 4 weeks before enrollment, with dose changes ≤ 20%.
* Adequately controlled blood pressure (≤140/90 mmHg) and fasting blood glucose (≤6.1 mmol/L), with stable vital signs.
* Willing to receive Chinese herbal treatment and undergo scheduled follow-up assessments, including T-cell subset analysis, cytokine measurements, and renal function tests.
* Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) syndrome differentiation consistent with the indications for the AI-selected herbal formula.
* Female participants who are not pregnant and agree to use effective contraception during the study.
* Willing and able to provide written informed consent.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Acute transplant rejection within the past 3 months or rapidly progressive IgA nephropathy (eGFR decline ≥30%).
* Severe renal impairment (eGFR \<30 mL/min/1.73 m²) or requiring dialysis.
* Severe proteinuria (\>3.5 g/day) or nephrotic syndrome.
* Active infections, including opportunistic infections, active hepatitis B or C infection, or active tuberculosis.
* Initiation or major dose adjustment of immunosuppressants, biologic agents, or corticosteroids, or antibiotic treatment within the past 4 weeks.
* History of malignancy within the past 5 years.
* Severe cardiovascular, hepatic, hematologic, or psychiatric disorders that may affect study participation or adherence.
* Known allergy or hypersensitivity to any component or excipient of the study herbal formula.
* Pregnant or breastfeeding women, or women planning to become pregnant during the study period.
* Participation in another clinical trial during the study period.
